2.text: The Chukchee have little chance to split logs in their treeless country,

3.text: and indeed they prefer simply to hew wood with their light adzes, though

4.text: sometimes it takes a day to cut a single sledge-runner. They have learned,

5.text: however, from the Yukaghir, who have more skill in handling wood, how to

6.text: split wood by means of wedges made of the same material.

7.text: WORK IN IRON. — Work in iron has been but little developed up to the

8.text: present time. This is explained by the difficulty in preparing charcoal, an

9.text: indispensable material for the smith. The Chukchee work chiefly on cold iron

10.text: with file and hammer (Plate XX, Fig. 2). A few clay forges with large bellows
